video_title: Robert Williams III Media Availability | Oct. 18, 2026 | Portland Trail Blazers

quotes.speaker: Robert Williams III
quotes.summary_phrase: Robert Williams III on his health and availability for the season
quotes.excerpt: Best stability is availability. Danny told me that a while ago, and I'm available, so keep that goal.
quotes.quote: I'm in a good spot. Been trusting the trainers. I give them all the praise along with my hard work. Best stability is availability. Danny told me that a while ago, and I'm available, so keep that goal.
quotes.social_post: Robert Williams III says he is in a good spot physically and is focused on staying on the court this season. He credits the training staff and his own hard work, noting that for him, the best stability is availability.

quotes.speaker: Robert Williams III
quotes.summary_phrase: Robert Williams III on the team's progress and hunger
quotes.excerpt: I feel like we got a long way to go, obviously, but I feel like we're hungry.
quotes.quote: I feel like we got a long way to go, obviously, but I feel like we're hungry. We don't expect sympathy from anyone. Everyone coming in here to take our heads off, which we want to do the same. I feel like everyone is rising to the challenge, challenging each other, bigger than anything. But we need to rebound. That's it, start with the bigs, but we need to rebound.
quotes.social_post: Robert Williams III says the Blazers are hungry and ready to compete. He emphasized that the team is not looking for sympathy and that the primary focus for the bigs right now is improving their rebounding.

quotes.speaker: Robert Williams III
quotes.summary_phrase: Robert Williams III on defensive communication and accountability
quotes.excerpt: Whatever the coverage is, whether you mess it up, whether it's a veer, and it shouldn't have been.
quotes.quote: Whatever the coverage is, whether you mess it up, whether it's a veer, and it shouldn't have been a veer, it's on us to lead the guards defensively. So whatever you call, they got to honor it. So just telling them like, even if you're indecisive, if you say something, even if you mess it up, mean it and go for it. To me, I think Michael is getting way better defensively, getting great at walling up, not swiping down, contesting shots.
quotes.social_post: Robert Williams III is pushing for better defensive communication from the Blazers. He says the bigs need to lead the guards and that players should be decisive with their calls even if they make a mistake.

quotes.speaker: Robert Williams III
quotes.summary_phrase: Robert Williams III on the development of teammate
quotes.excerpt: Hanson was a baby, he's still a baby, but you know he's a baby when he got here.
quotes.quote: Hanson was a baby, he's still a baby, but you know he's a baby when he got here. You get dropped off over here, you're going to have a tough time adjusting too. But I think he's growing up, turning into that man, and that comes with adding stuff on the court.
quotes.social_post: Robert Williams III sees growth in his younger teammates, noting that adjusting to the league is difficult but that they are starting to turn into men on the court.

quotes.speaker: Robert Williams III
quotes.summary_phrase: Robert Williams III on the team's culture of sacrifice
quotes.excerpt: The only selfish person on this team is Shaden. No, I'm talking, I'm talking.
quotes.quote: The only selfish person on this team is Shaden. No, I'm talking, I'm talking. But you know man, we were just talking about sacrifices for the team. One win, we all win. I feel like that's the biggest goal. We understand that, especially the late run we had last year going into the playoffs. One win, we all win.
quotes.social_post: Robert Williams III says the Blazers are focused on a culture of sacrifice this season. He believes the team understands that one win is a win for everyone, a mindset he says carried over from their late run last year.
